AccessScheduleRecurrenceRuleV2.description:
RFC 5545-style recurrence rule for a weekly Access Schedule Event.

Access Levels store a single weekday per schedule event and repeat forever,
so the rule carries only the three RRULE parts that shape has: ``WEEKLY``
frequency, an interval of one week, and the one weekday it falls on. Any
other recurrence part is rejected rather than silently ignored.

not need to be duplicated here.

CloudBackupSettingsPatchRequestV2.description:
A partial update to a camera's cloud backup settings.

Every field is optional; the ones supplied are applied and the rest are left
as they are. Because none of these fields is nullable, an omitted field and
an explicit ``null`` mean the same thing -- leave it alone.

backup_days.description: The days of the week whose footage is backed up, as full weekday names (for example ["Monday", "Tuesday"]). An empty list backs up no days. Replaces the existing list rather than adding to it.

backup_window.description: The daily window of footage that is backed up. Footage recorded outside this window is not uploaded. Both ends must be supplied together.
backup_window.title: Backup Window

enabled.description: Whether cloud backup is enabled for the camera. Re-enabling a camera whose backup was previously disabled resumes from the time it was disabled.
enabled.title: Enabled

upload_window.description: The daily window during which uploads are allowed to run. Both ends must be supplied together.
upload_window.title: Upload Window

video_quality.description: The quality the footage is uploaded at. Either STANDARD_QUALITY or HIGH_QUALITY.

video_to_upload.description: Which footage inside the backup window is uploaded. MOTION uploads only footage containing motion; ALL uploads every recorded second.

NJSnapPOI.description:
A single POI record from the NJ SNAP Hotlist feed.

Always required: `ID`, `Status`, `PlateNumber` — the spec highlights PlateNumber as
mandatory in all three schemas (§4.1 ADD, §5.1 EDIT, §6.1 DELETE), and §6.1 states a DELETE
"will be a full record to coincide with the Unique identifier of the original record".
`PlateSt` is required for `ADD`/`EDIT` only, since those write a document that needs a state.
Mirrors vsight's validate_pois, so the two layers accept the same inputs.

All other fields are optional. Extra undocumented fields (e.g. `DeptORI`, `DeptName`,
`EntryDate`, which appear in the spec examples but not the schema) are preserved via
`extra = "allow"` so downstream consumers can stash them.

PlateSt.title: Platest

NJSnapPOIBatchRequestV2.description:
Inbound request body — `{"POIs": [...]}` per spec §4.1.

No upper bound on batch size: the spec places none, and NJ SNAP's queue-and-flush-on-
reconnect design (see the POI Hits/Entries addendum) can legitimately replay a large
backlog in one push. NJSnapPOIHandlerV2 chunks the batch into <=MAX_POIS_PER_REQUEST
sub-batches when forwarding to vsight, per the vpublicapi convention of chunking
unbounded downstream calls rather than rejecting large inputs outright.

RecurrenceFrequencyV2.description:
Recurrence frequencies supported by Access Schedule Events.

The downstream Access Level representation is intrinsically weekly, so this
resource supports the RFC 5545 ``WEEKLY`` frequency only.
RecurrenceFrequencyV2.title: RecurrenceFrequencyV2

RecurrenceRule.description: A recurrence rule object specifying when the exception should repeat.

by_day.description: For recurrences where frequency is WEEKLY, MONTHLY, or YEARLY. List of weekdays that the recurrence should include every week (see BYDAY in RFC 5545). Supported values are: 'SU', 'MO', 'TU', 'WE', 'TH', 'FR', 'SA'. Note: Required if frequency is WEEKLY, and can include one or more values. If frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY, only allowed if by_set_pos is not null and can only include a single value. Not supported otherwise.

by_month.description: For recurrences where frequency is YEARLY. The number of the month that the recurrence should include every year (see BYMONTH in RFC 5545). Supported values are integers from 1-12. Note: Required if frequency is YEARLY, not supported otherwise.
by_month.title: By Month

by_month_day.description: For recurrences where frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY. The day of the month that the recurrence should include every month or year (see BYMONTHDAY in RFC 5545). Supported values are integers from 1-31. If the value is set to 29-31 and a month does not include a day with that value, the recurrence will be ignored for that month. Note: Either by_month_day or by_set_pos is required if frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY (only one is allowed), not supported otherwise.
by_month_day.title: By Month Day

by_set_pos.description: For recurrences where frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY. The position of the weekday specified in by_day in the month that the recurrence should include every month or year (see BYMONTHDAY in RFC 5545). For example, by_set_pos would be set to 3 and by_day set to 'TU', to specify the 3rd Tuesday of a month. Supported values are integers from 1-5. If value is set to 5 and the month does not include a 5th instance of the weekday in by_day, the recurrence will be ignored for that month. Note: Either by_month_day or by_set_pos is required if frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY (only one is allowed). Not supported otherwise.
by_set_pos.title: By Set Pos

count.description: The total number of times that the recurrence should repeat before ending (see COUNT in RFC 5545). Note: Only one of count or until is allowed, but not both.
count.title: Count

excluded_dates.description: A list of dates to exclude for recurrence, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD (according to ISO 8601). Also see EXDATE in RFC 5545.
excluded_dates.title: Excluded Dates

frequency.description: Frequency type of the recurrence (see FREQ in RFC 5545). Supported values are: 'DAILY', 'WEEKLY', 'MONTHLY', 'YEARLY'.

interval.description: Interval at which the recurrence should repeat according to the frequency type (see INTERVAL in RFC 5545).
interval.title: Interval

until.description: The final date on which the recurrence should occur before ending, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD (according to ISO 8601). Also see UNTIL in RFC 5545. Note: Only one of count or until is allowed, but not both.
until.title: Until

RecurrenceRule.title: RecurrenceRule

RecurrenceRuleV2.description: A recurrence rule object specifying when the exception should repeat (RFC 5545).

by_day.description: For recurrences where frequency is WEEKLY, MONTHLY, or YEARLY. List of weekday names (full strings such as Monday) on which the recurrence should repeat (see BYDAY in RFC 5545). Required when frequency is WEEKLY. When frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY, only allowed if by_set_pos is set, and may contain only a single weekday.

by_month.description: For recurrences where frequency is YEARLY. The month number on which the recurrence should repeat (see BYMONTH in RFC 5545). Supported values are 1-12. Required when frequency is YEARLY.
by_month.title: By Month

by_set_pos.description: For recurrences where frequency is MONTHLY or YEARLY. The position of the weekday specified in by_day within the month (see BYSETPOS in RFC 5545). For example, set by_set_pos to 3 and by_day to ['Tuesday'] to specify the third Tuesday of a month. Supported values are 1-5.

frequency.description: Frequency type of the recurrence (see FREQ in RFC 5545). Supported values: DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, YEARLY.

interval.description: Interval at which the recurrence repeats according to the frequency type (see INTERVAL in RFC 5545). Must be greater than 0.
interval.title: Interval

until.description: The final date on which the recurrence should occur, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601). See UNTIL in RFC 5545. Only one of count or until is allowed.

UpdateAccessLevelRequestV2.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v2/access/access_levels/<access_level_id>`.

Every field is optional. Only the fields present in the request body are
changed; omitted fields keep their current value.

``access_schedule_events`` is deliberately absent: the weekly windows of an
Access Level are managed exclusively through the nested
``/v2/access/access_levels/<access_level_id>/access_schedule_events``
endpoints. Supplying ``access_schedule_events`` here is a validation error.
This differs from the v1 ``PUT`` endpoint, which required the complete event
list on every update.

access_groups.description: The complete replacement list of Access Group identifiers granted door access by this Access Level.

doors.description: The complete replacement list of Door identifiers accessible under this Access Level. Every Door must belong to one of the Access Level's Sites.

name.description: The new name of the Access Level. Must be unique within the organization, at most 100 characters, and must not contain any of the characters `<>{}[]`.
name.title: Name

sites.description: The complete replacement list of Site identifiers containing the Doors this Access Level applies to. At least one Site is required, and every Site must be within the scope of the API key.
sites.title: Sites

UpdateAccessScheduleEventRequestV2.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v2/access/access_levels/<access_level_id>/access_schedule_events/<event_id>`.

Every field is optional. Only the fields present in the request body are
changed; omitted fields keep their current value. This differs from the v1
`PUT` endpoint, which replaced the whole event and therefore required
`recurrence_rule`, `start_time`, and `end_time` on every request.

door_status.description: The status applied to the doors while the event is active. Only `access_granted` is supported. Omit to leave the status unchanged.

end_time.description: The new local time at which the event ends, in 24-hour `HH:MM` format with leading zeros (`00:00` through `23:59`). Omit to leave the end time unchanged.
end_time.title: End Time

recurrence_rule.description: The new RFC 5545-style weekly recurrence rule. Omit to leave the recurrence unchanged.
recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule

start_time.description: The new local time at which the event starts, in 24-hour `HH:MM` format with leading zeros (`00:00` through `23:59`). Omit to leave the start time unchanged.
start_time.title: Start Time

get.description:
Introduction: Although many Verkada customers access camera footage via Command, we offer a flexible solution for integrating third-party applications with Verkada cameras. Streaming API allows users to stream both live and historical footage from cameras using the HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) protocol. HLS is an open protocol designed for streaming media content over the internet, supported by many video players. This document serves as a guide for integrating camera footage into third-party applications. Prerequisites: Before integrating with the Streaming API, ensure you have the following:
  1. Access to the Verkada API. Read our Quick Start Guide
  2. An application equipped with a video player capable of streaming via HLS protocol (i.e HLS.js)
  3. A backend server capable of communicating with Verkada API servers
Steps to Stream Footage: Follow these steps to stream footage using the Streaming API: Step 1: Acquire a JSON Web Token (JWT) via Get Streaming Token endpoint To access the streaming endpoint, obtain a JWT via the Get Streaming Token endpoint. While the streaming endpoint doesn't require an API Key, it requires a valid JWT as a query parameter for streaming footage. Step 2: Assemble the API endpoint URL Construct the full API endpoint URL with the necessary parameters. Determine whether you're streaming live or historical footage, specify the resolution (low or high), identify the camera, and identify the organization. Refer to the parameter documentation for detailed specifications. Certain parameters must have a single value, while others don't need to be manually specified. Ensure all parameters have the correct values. Upon completing this step, you will have a fully constructed URL for the endpoint, which will return an m3u8 playlist file in response. Note: Specify the key as stream.m3u8 to start HLS streaming for live or historical footage. Step 3: Call the endpoint to stream footage Once you've assembled the endpoint URL, you can either directly call the endpoint or let compatible video players handle the streaming process. Most HLS-compatible players will automatically interact with the endpoint, manage the m3u8 playlist response, and request subsequent video segments. Alternatively, if you want to directly handle the m3u8 playlist output in your frontend code, you can parse the list of video segment files and render footage according to your application's requirements. Response Codes:
Response Code Message Troubleshooting Steps
500 Failed authentication step Check if a valid JSON web token was submitted.
500 Internal Server Error Verkada's server might be experiencing issues. Submit a support ticket if it fails repeatedly.
500 Error Fetching Live Video m3u8 Check if all query parameters have correct values.
500 Error Fetching Historical Video m3u8 Check if all query parameters have correct values and the footage needed (i.e. timestamp specified) is within the camera's days of retention.
500 Error Fetching Live Video Init mp4 File Check if all query parameters have correct values.
500 Error Fetching Historical Video Init mp4 File Check if all query parameters have correct values and the footage needed (i.e. timestamp specified) is within the camera's days of retention.
500 Error Fetching Historical Video m4s File Check if all query parameters have correct values.
500 Error Fetching Live Video m4s File Check if all query parameters have correct values.
500 Error Fetching Historical Video Encryption Key Check if all query parameters have correct values.
For standard HTTP response codes, refer to our General Troubleshooting page.

post.description: API Tokens are required to make requests to any Verkada API endpoints with the exception of the Get Streaming Token endpoints, which requires a top-level API Key for authentication, as well as the Stream Footage (live or historical) API that requires a JSON Web Token (JWT). API Tokens inherit permissions from the top-level API key used to generate them and will be limited to that same permission scope. If the API Key used to generate an API Token only has Camera Read-Only permissions, then the associated API Token would only be authorized to call Camera GET endpoints. API Tokens are valid for 30 minutes and cannot be refreshed. Users will need to call the Get API Token endpoint again to retrieve a new Token if their previous one has expired. When making a call using an expired API Token, users will receive a 401 Authentication Error as well as the following error message: {'id': '0e2d', 'message': 'Token expired', 'data': None}

Returns a paginated list of the Access Levels the API key can see, each
including the weekly schedule events during which it grants access. Only
Access Levels whose Sites are within the API key's scope are returned.

next request, and stop once `cursor` is `null`.

post.description:
Creates an Access Level granting the given Access Groups entry to the given
Doors during the given weekly schedule events. Every Site listed in `sites`
must be within the API key's scope, and every Door in `doors` must belong to
one of those Sites.

The name must be unique within the organization; a collision returns 409.
Two schedule events on the same weekday must not overlap or touch -- the
later one must start strictly after the earlier one ends; a violation returns
422.

delete.description:
Deletes the Access Level with the given identifier. Deleting requires
permission to remove Access Levels on every Site the Access Level belongs to;
a caller without that permission, or an Access Level outside the API key's
scope, returns 404.

get.description:
Retrieves the Access Level with the given identifier, including the weekly
schedule events during which it grants access. An Access Level whose Sites
fall outside the API key's scope returns 404.

patch.description:
Applies a partial update to the Access Level with the given identifier. Only
the fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields keep their
current value. Provide at least one field.

`access_groups`, `sites`, and `doors` are each replaced wholesale when
supplied, so send the complete intended list rather than only the additions.

The Access Level's weekly schedule events cannot be changed here; they are
managed by the nested `access_schedule_events` endpoints and are preserved
across every update. This differs from the v1 endpoint, where the full event
list had to be resent with every update.

A name that collides with another Access Level returns 409. Requesting a Site
outside the API key's scope returns 404.

post.description:
Adds a weekly window to the given Access Level, during which the Access Level
grants its Access Groups entry to its Doors.

The new window must not overlap or touch a window already on the Access Level
for the same weekday -- it must start strictly after the other window ends;
a violation returns 422. An Access Level whose Sites fall outside the API
key's scope returns 404.

delete.description:
Removes a single weekly window from the given Access Level. The Access Level
itself is left in place, even if the deleted window was its last one, in which
case the Access Level grants no access until a window is added back.

get.description:
Retrieves a single weekly window from the given Access Level. An Access Level
or event that does not exist, or an Access Level whose Sites fall outside the
API key's scope, returns 404.

patch.description:
Applies a partial update to a single weekly window on the given Access Level.
Only the fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields keep
their current value, so changing the end time alone does not require resending
the recurrence rule and start time. Provide at least one field.

This differs from the v1 endpoint, where the weekday, start time, and end time
all had to be resent on every update.

The updated window must not overlap or touch another window on the Access
Level for the same weekday, and its end time must fall strictly after its
start time; a violation returns 422.

get.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of doors in the organization. The response can optionally
be filtered to doors within sites with the requested `site_ids` or to the specific
doors represented by the specified `door_ids`. Only one of `site_ids` or `door_ids`
can be used to filter the response for a single request (not both).

### Pagination

This endpoint uses cursor-based pagination:
- **`limit`**: Number of doors to return per page (1-1000, default 100).
- **`cursor`**: Pagination cursor returned by a previous response.
- Continue paginating while the response contains a non-null `cursor`.

### Examples

Get all doors in the organization:
```
GET /v2/access/doors
```

Filter by site:
```
GET /v2/access/doors?site_ids=<site_uuid>
```

Filter by specific doors:
```
GET /v2/access/doors?door_ids=<door_uuid_1>,<door_uuid_2>
```

Paginate:
```
GET /v2/access/doors?limit=50
GET /v2/access/doors?limit=50&cursor=<cursor_from_previous_response>
```

get.description:
Introduction: Although many Verkada customers access camera footage via Command, we offer a flexible solution for integrating third-party applications with Verkada cameras. The Streaming API lets you stream both live and historical footage from cameras using the HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) protocol. HLS is an open protocol for streaming media over the internet, supported by many video players. This document is a guide for integrating camera footage into third-party applications. Prerequisites: Before integrating with the Streaming API, ensure you have the following:
  1. Access to the Verkada API. Read our Quick Start Guide
  2. An application equipped with a video player capable of streaming via the HLS protocol (for example HLS.js)
  3. A backend server capable of communicating with Verkada API servers
Steps to Stream Footage: Step 1: Acquire a JSON Web Token (JWT) from the Get Streaming Token endpoint. This endpoint does not take an API key. It takes a valid JWT as the jwt query parameter, which the token endpoint issues against your API key. Step 2: Assemble the endpoint URL. Decide whether you are streaming live or historical footage, choose the resolution, and identify the camera and the organization. For live footage, leave start_time and end_time at 0. For historical footage, set both; they may be ISO 8601 timestamps (2025-07-17T21:06:20Z) or epoch seconds, and may span at most one hour. Set the key path parameter to stream.m3u8 to begin HLS streaming. Step 3: Call the endpoint. Most HLS-compatible players will take the returned m3u8 playlist and request the subsequent segments themselves. The segment URLs inside the playlist are relative and already carry every parameter they need, so they resolve back to this endpoint without further work. Alternatively, parse the playlist yourself and fetch the segments directly. Error Responses: Errors are returned in the standard v2 error shape, carrying a stable error_code alongside the support code id.
Response Code error_code Troubleshooting Steps
400 bad_request Check the query parameters. resolution must be low_res or high_res, codec must be hevc or h264, and start_time and end_time must either both be 0 (live) or both be set and no more than an hour apart (historical).
401 unauthorized Check that a valid, unexpired JWT was submitted in the jwt query parameter.
403 forbidden The token does not grant streaming access to this camera, or the Streaming API is not enabled for the organization.
404 object_not_found Check that org_id and camera_id are correct and that the camera belongs to the organization.
500 internal_error Verkada's servers may be experiencing issues, or the requested footage is outside the camera's retention window. Submit a support ticket, quoting the id from the response body, if it fails repeatedly.
For standard HTTP response codes, refer to our General Troubleshooting page.

get.description:
Returns a low-resolution or high-resolution thumbnail from a specified
camera at or near a specified time.

The `timestamp` query parameter is an ISO 8601 string and defaults to
the current time. Defaults to low-resolution thumbnails.

`start_time` and `end_time` optionally bound the search window used to find
the thumbnail; if omitted, the search covers one hour either side of
`timestamp`. The window may not exceed four hours. They are not supported
when `resolution` is hi-res.

The response includes an `X-Verkada-Timestamp` header with the Unix timestamp
of the actual capture time of the frame served.

Returns a low-resolution thumbnail if this parameter is set to 'low-res'.
Returns a high-resolution thumbnail if this parameter is set to 'hi-res'.

Defaults to a low-resolution thumbnail.

The inclusive start of the time window to search for a thumbnail, formatted as an ISO 8601 string (e.g. '2025-07-17T20:06:20Z').

If omitted, the search covers one hour either side of `timestamp`.

The window between `start_time` and `end_time` may not exceed four hours.

`start_time` and `end_time` must be specified together.

Not supported when `resolution` is hi-res.

schema.description:

`start_time` and `end_time` must be specified together.

Not supported when `resolution` is hi-res.
schema.title: End Time

get.description:
Returns a link to a thumbnail image from a specified camera at a
specified time.

Accepts the capture `timestamp` as an ISO 8601 datetime
(e.g., 2025-07-17T21:06:20Z) and the link `expiry` as an ISO 8601
duration (e.g., PT1H, P1D). Returns the capture time and link expiry
as RFC 3339 timestamps.

Optionally accepts `start_time` and `end_time` as ISO 8601 datetimes
to bound the search window for the returned thumbnail: instead of the
closest snapshot to `timestamp`, the nearest snapshot within
`[start_time, end_time]` is returned. `start_time` and `end_time`
must be specified together, and the window between them may not
exceed four hours. If omitted, the endpoint keeps its existing
behavior.

schema.description: How long the generated link stays valid, as an ISO 8601 duration (e.g., PT1H for one hour, P1D for one day). Must be between one hour and one week. Defaults to one day (P1D).
schema.title: Expiry

schema.description:
The inclusive start of the time window to search for a thumbnail, formatted as an ISO 8601 string (e.g. '2025-07-17T20:06:20Z').

`start_time` and `end_time` must be specified together.

The window between `start_time` and `end_time` may not exceed four hours.

If omitted, the endpoint keeps its existing behavior.
schema.title: Start Time

schema.description:

`start_time` and `end_time` must be specified together.

The window between `start_time` and `end_time` may not exceed four hours.

If omitted, the endpoint keeps its existing behavior.

post.description:
Searches for license plate detection events within a specified time range
and geographic area.

**Access Restriction**: This endpoint is only available to organizations with
CJIS (Criminal Justice Information Services) access enabled. Contact Verkada
support to enable this feature for your organization.

### Search Capabilities

**Plate Search with Wildcards**:

Use the `license_plate` field with wildcard (`*`) support for flexible matching:
- `ABC123` - Exact match
- `ABC*` - Starts with "ABC"
- `*123` - Ends with "123"
- `*BC1*` - Contains "BC1"

**Geographic Filtering**:
- `geo_fence`: Define a polygon (3-700 coordinate pairs) to filter events
  by camera location. Only events from cameras within the polygon are returned.

**Time Range**:
- Maximum query range is 3 years
- Results are returned in reverse chronological order (newest first)

### Response Fields

Each result includes:
- `read_id`: Unique identifier for the detection event
- `plate`: The detected license plate number
- `plate_state`: Two-character state code (may be null)
- `lat`/`lon`: Camera location coordinates
- `event_time`: Detection timestamp in RFC 3339 format
- `image_data`: URL to the license plate image
- `additional_image`: URL to the full vehicle image
- `agency_name`: Name of the organization owning the camera
- `ori`: Originating Agency Identifier (for NCIC events)

### Pagination

Use cursor-based pagination:
- Set `limit` to control page size (1-1000, default 100)
- Use the returned `cursor` value in subsequent requests to get more results
- Continue until `cursor` is null

### Example Request

```json
{
    "start_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_time": "2025-01-15T23:59:59Z",
    "license_plate": "*ABC*",
    "geo_fence": [
        {"latitude": 37.7749, "longitude": -122.4194},
        {"latitude": 37.7849, "longitude": -122.4094},
        {"latitude": 37.7649, "longitude": -122.4094}
    ],
    "limit": 100
}
```

|------|-------------|

| 401 | The API credential is missing or invalid |
| 403 | The API credential lacks camera write permission |
| 404 | No such camera in this organization |

put.description:

and the call replaces the settings in full, so a value that is omitted
is not left as it was.

Re-enabling backup on a camera whose backup was previously enabled and
then disabled resumes from the time it was disabled, rather than
starting from the present.

The response is the set of settings now in effect.

### Error Responses

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 400 | The request failed validation |
| 401 | The API credential is missing or invalid |
| 403 | The API credential lacks camera write permission |
| 404 | No such camera in this organization |

Returns audit logs for an organization within a specified time range.

All audit logs include a timestamp in ISO 8601 date time format, user info, IP
address, event info, and device info.

### Pagination

This endpoint uses cursor-based pagination:
- **`limit`**: The number of audit logs to return (1-200, default 100).
- **`cursor`**: The pagination cursor from a previous response used to fetch the
  next page. Continue paginating while the response includes a non-null `cursor`.

For a stable result set, set an explicit `end_time`. If `end_time` is omitted it
defaults to the current time on each request, so audit logs written while you are
paginating can shift entries between pages (a page boundary may repeat or skip
entries). Pinning `end_time` to a fixed instant avoids this.

get.description:
Returns unified events from camera, access control, and sensor devices within a specified time range.

This endpoint consolidates events from camera, access control, and sensor devices in your organization,
providing a single interface to retrieve security events, access control events, and environmental sensor events.

**Default Behavior**: Returns events from all supported product types from the last hour if no filters are specified.

### Supported Event Types

**Camera Events:**
- `camera_online`, `camera_offline` - Camera connectivity status
- `motion` - Motion detection events
- `person_of_interest` - Person of Interest detections
- `license_plate_of_interest` - License Plate of Interest detections
- `tamper` - Camera tampering events
- `crowd` - Crowd detection events
- `line_crossing` - Line crossing rule violations
- `loitering` - Loitering/dwell time violations
- `inactivity` - Inactivity/no-motion alert violations

**Access Control Events:**
- `door_opened`, `door_granted`, `door_rejected` - Access events
- `door_forced_open`, `door_held_open` - Security violations
- `door_tailgating` - Tailgating detection
- `door_tamper` - Door tampering events
- `door_offline` - Access control unit connectivity
- Plus 50+ additional access control event types for comprehensive monitoring

**Sensor Events:**
- `temperature`, `humidity` - Climate monitoring alerts
- `tvoc`, `co2`, `pm25` - Air quality alerts
- `noise` - Noise level alerts
- `sensor_motion` - Motion detection from sensors
- `air_quality` - General air quality alerts

### Filtering

Use these query parameters to filter results:
- **`product_types`**: Comma-separated product types (`camera`, `access_control`, `sensor`)
- **`device_ids`**: Comma-separated list of device IDs to filter by
- **`event_types`**: Comma-separated list of event types (see supported types above)
- **`start_time`**: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., `2025-01-17T09:00:00Z`)
- **`end_time`**: End time in ISO 8601 format (defaults to current time if not specified)
- **`site_ids`**: Comma-separated list of site IDs (for access control events)

### Pagination

This endpoint uses cursor-based pagination with these parameters:
- **`limit`**: Number of events to return (1-1000, default 100)
- **`cursor`**: Pagination cursor from previous response for next page
- Continue paginating while the response includes a `cursor` value



### Examples

Get all events from the last hour:
```
GET /v2/events
```

Get only camera motion events from a specific time range:
```
GET /v2/events?product_types=camera&event_types=motion&start_time=2025-01-17T09:00:00Z&end_time=2025-01-17T17:00:00Z
```

Get access control events for specific doors:
```
GET /v2/events?product_types=access_control&device_ids=door1,door2&limit=50
```

Get sensor temperature and humidity alerts:
```
GET /v2/events?product_types=sensor&event_types=temperature,humidity&start_time=2025-01-17T09:00:00Z
```
